courses.title: Applied Behavior Design Wrkshp
courses.course_description: Learn to apply behavioral science to real-world challenges. This workshop teaches you evidence-based methods for understanding behavior—including literature reviews, COM-B analysis, and evaluative testing—and shows you how to use them in practical design work. You'll develop skills in combining behavioral research with design strategies and systems thinking to create solutions that address individual, institutional, and system-level behaviors. Students may take this course multiple times, non-concurrently, for a maximum of 12 credits towards the MDes degree.

courses.title: Intro to Systems Theory
courses.course_description: The course investigates principles and methods for representing and understanding structure and behavior of different types of systems. Various forms of theoretical and philosophical frameworks and methodologies are introduced to model and understand fundamental characteristics of domains of concern from different perspectives. Class topics include general systems theory, system modeling, causality, and formalisms. The class will also explore example applications of system concepts and modeling methods in design research.
